scope_note: SG-MA-PUBLIC-HEALTH-STANDING-ORDERS after corrections following the V10B audit. Board Policy 2024-01 (revised 2/6/2025) states that all areas of Massachusetts have high rates of opioid overdose or death, so Massachusetts pharmacies must stock naloxone under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19C and keep a continuous, sufficient supply; the Board's retail inspection form (item 60) checks it and the July 13, 2026 standing order refers pharmacists to the policy, while 247 CMR 9.06 still ties the duty to a Board-published list. The section now presents that question as arguable and gives the course safe on either reading, a continuous supply in every Massachusetts pharmacy. Reporting under Policy section II (doses, preferably through the daily prescription monitoring program submission, otherwise an annual e-mailed report by January 15) is taught as policy. Counseling and the pamphlet now attach only to dispensing on a prescription or the standing order, because 247 CMR 2.00 defines dispensing as delivery pursuant to a practitioner's lawful order and the Department's 12/20/2023 memo says retailers should allow anonymous open-shelf purchase of nonprescription naloxone. New rules: MA-NALOXONE-STATEWIDE-STOCKING-POLICY, MA-NALOXONE-DOSE-REPORTING-POLICY, MA-DISPENSING-DEFINITION and MA-OTC-NALOXONE-SHELF-ACCESS. Scope gate: all 17 actionable signals declined; they are administration (MA-ADMIN-*, MA-PHARMACY-IMMUNIZATION-ADMINISTRATION), collaborative drug therapy management prescribing (MA-CDTM-*, MA-PHARMACIST-PRESCRIBER-ID) and contraception (MA-HORMONAL-CONTRACEPTIVE) records that neighbouring sections teach or will teach, and orientation[8] points to them.
